question_type: Count of data cells with leading digit 1 across the table(s) on a pinned report page of a pinned issue

opus_path.decision: Issue = May 1980; page = printed report page 23; count every data cell (not row labels or column headers) whose first digit is 1; output one integer.
Issue and page are pinned, so there is no vintage question.
Read the issue's Contents: UST-3 is on p.22, MS-1 on p.23, FD-1 on p.24, so page 23 holds only MS-1.
Bounded page 23 with running-header markers: 'May 1980' / '23' at 1704-1706 opens the page, '24' at 1777 opens the next. MS-1 is printed as two column blocks, and 'tables' means both blocks.
Checked the OCR by row/column sums in both blocks and by comparing with the April and June 1980 MS-1 printings, ruling out column shifts.
Rules: strip commas, footnote markers ('7/') and revision flags ('r'); '*' cells contain no numeral. Tallied per column, including a small column whose every cell is a bare '1'.
Counted in calc.py, then cross-checked against the manual per-column tally.
Considered whether another table shares the page (no, per the page markers) and excluded row-label years.

opus_key_moves: Mapped report page 23 to its content using BOTH the Contents listing and the running-header page markers, which puts the page-22 table (UST-3) outside the page (worklog.md:13-27)
Counted both column blocks of MS-1, including the all-'1' single-digit column (worklog.md:40-51)

none.right_arms_note: Read the file head to line 120 [17], so it saw the Contents entry placing MS-1 on page 23 ([18] 'Contents says MS-1 page 23'), located MS-1 by title [21]-[22], and counted both blocks.

first_divergence.what_glm_did: Grepped only for a bare '23' line [12] (hit at line 1706), printed lines 1620-1760 [13], and assigned the table ABOVE that marker (UST-3, Gold Assets and Liabilities) to page 23, treating the page number as a footer. It counted UST-3's cells only.
first_divergence.what_opus_did: Read the Contents (UST-3 = p.22, MS-1 = p.23) and treated 'May 1980 / 23' as the running header that OPENS page 23, bounded by '24' at line 1777 (worklog.md:13-27).
first_divergence.why_glm_went_that_way: Its first look at the file ([9], sed 1-80) stopped a few lines before the Contents entries for pages 22-23, so it never saw the TOC mapping. It never searched for the '22' marker that sits just above the UST-3 title (corpus line 1661). At [16] it asserted 'page 22 at line 1705, page 23 at 1706', a misreading of the marker layout.
first_divergence.consequence: Counted the wrong table (the page-22 table), and the count is ~48% below Opus's.

saw_correct_evidence.where: [13]: its own output shows 'May 1980', '23', 'MONETARY STATISTICS', 'Table MS-1. - Currency and Coin in Circulation' and MS-1 rows directly after the marker

glm_expressed_doubt.where: [14] and [16]: questioned the plural 'tables' and whether page 41 maps to page 23 ('But ensure page 41 corresponds printed page 23'), then resolved both without checking the Contents

operational.tool_friction: rg blocked [3]; string index/rindex slicing bugs while isolating the table [22]-[29]
operational.notes: 17 requests, 131 s; 1.5M input tokens, dominated by the 221 KB adapter.

adapter_context.notes: The adapter had no lesson on page-number mapping or page-scoped counting questions.

remedies.intervention: Page helper docs.page(filename, report_page=N) that returns the text between running-header marker N and marker N+1, plus the Contents entries listed at page N.
remedies.why: The error was purely page-to-text mapping. With the page slice returned, UST-3 would not be in view, and MS-1 was already visible at [13].

remedies.intervention: Page-claim checker: when the actor commits to 'table T is on report page N', verify that T's title appears in that issue's Contents with page N (or lies between markers N and N+1); on mismatch, return the Contents line for page N.
remedies.why: The Contents lists UST-3 at 22 and MS-1 at 23 (1980_05.txt:84-88), so the check fires deterministically on the [14]/[17] claim.

remedies.intervention: Convention note: 'In these TXT files page numbers are running HEADERS at the top of a page (odd pages: issue date then number; even pages: number then Treasury Bulletin). Page N's content lies between marker N and marker N+1. Confirm with the Contents list.'
remedies.why: The two right arms reached this reading unaided, and the prompt arm had no such text. But the prompt arm often ignores text in its 220 KB context, so a mechanism is more reliable.

cards.right_arms_note: Bounded page 23 between the '23' and '24' running-header markers ([13] 'Output starts page 22 and then page 23', [15]-[17]), took both MS-1 blocks, and caught its own script bug that dropped bare '1' cells ([28]-[30]).

right_arms_note: none used the Contents listing (it read the file head to line 120, and the TOC entry for MS-1 sits just past line 80). cards read the page markers as headers and located the next-page marker. The prompt arm read only lines 1-80, grepped only for '23', and treated the marker as a footer.
text_vs_mechanism: A text convention would plausibly fix this: the prompt arm had no relevant text, and the right arms reasoned correctly without any. A page-slice tool or a Contents-based page-claim check would make it robust, and it would be cheap because the TOC is in every issue.
notes: (1) Near miss in the right arms: cards' first script silently skipped single-digit '1' cells, and it only caught this by eyeballing the match list. A CHECK that reports per-column cell counts, numeric-parse failures, and the per-column tally would make counting questions safer. (2) Page-pinned questions are a recurring OfficeQA family. A deterministic page slicer keyed on report page, with a pdf-to-report page offset learned per issue, is a high-leverage reusable TOOL. (3) The prompt arm's first file peek (head -80) stopping just short of the relevant TOC line is a pure-luck factor; a tool returning the whole Contents block would remove it.
